blocks.prompt: 9 Find the gradient and an equation of tangent line to the graph of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\) at \(x = 9\).
blocks.explanation:
A tangent to a square-root curve. The slope is \(f'(9)\), found by the limit at the point.
Plan: the difference quotient at \(x = 9\), rationalise, take the limit; then the point-slope form.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\), \(x_1 = 9\).
To find: the gradient \(f'(9)\) and the tangent line.
Method: first principles at the point: \(f'(9) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\frac{f(9 + \delta x) - f(9)}{\delta x}\), with rationalising. The gradient (slope) of the tangent at \(x = x_1\) is \(m = f'(x_1)\); the tangent is \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with \(y_1 = f(x_1)\).

The difference quotient at \(x = 9\)
\[\dfrac{f(9 + \delta x) - f(9)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{\sqrt{9 + \delta x} - 3}{\delta x}\]
Why: \(f(9) = \sqrt{9} = 3\).

Rationalise the top
\[= \dfrac{(\sqrt{9 + \delta x} - 3)(\sqrt{9 + \delta x} + 3)}{\delta x\,(\sqrt{9 + \delta x} + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{(9 + \delta x) - 9}{\delta x\,(\sqrt{9 + \delta x} + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9 + \delta x} + 3}\]
Why: \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\); then \(\delta x\) cancels (\(\delta x \neq 0\)).

Take the limit: the gradient
\[f'(9) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9 + \delta x} + 3}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3 + 3} = \dfrac{1}{6}\]
Why: The bottom tends to \(6\), not \(0\).

Point and equation of the tangent
\[(x_1, y_1) = (9, 3)\]
\[y - 3 = \dfrac{1}{6}(x - 9)\]
\[6y - 18 = x - 9\]
\[6y = x + 9\]
Why: Point-slope form; multiply by \(6\) to clear the fraction.

Check
\[x = 9:\ 6y = 18 \Rightarrow y = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sqrt{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{1}{6}\ \text{at}\ x = 9\]
Why: The line passes through \((9, 3)\); Question 1(ii)'s working gives the same slope.
